target_in_paper: Most likely Question 8.3.1 in §8.3 ("Generic metrics") of the current arXiv version: whether metrics whose geodesic flow has positive entropy are C^k-dense among smooth Riemannian metrics on a closed manifold. The draft is not uniquely identifying, because the same opening hypothesis also starts Questions 8.3.2 and 8.3.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly captures one genuine hypothesis from §8.3: the ambient manifold M is assumed to be closed. It also uses the paper’s ambient manifold notation M.
missing_details: The draft does not identify which of the three consecutive questions in §8.3 beginning with "Assume M is closed" is intended.
If the target is Question 8.3.1, the actual property under discussion is positive entropy of the geodesic flow.
The ambient space must be specified: the paper considers the space R^k(M) of all smooth Riemannian metrics on M.
The topology must be specified: R^k(M) carries the weak C^k-topology.
A fixed regularity parameter k must be included (the paper notes the question can be asked for any k).
The conclusion is a density statement: the subset of metrics with the stated dynamical property should be dense in R^k(M).
The object whose entropy is meant must be stated explicitly: it is the geodesic flow of the metric.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say that M is a closed smooth manifold, not merely "closed."
The draft omits the quantifier structure implicit in density: every metric in R^k(M) should be approximable arbitrarily well in the C^k-topology by metrics with the stated property.
refined_question: Let M be a closed smooth manifold, fix k in {0,1,2,...,∞}, and let R^k(M) denote the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on M endowed with the weak C^k-topology (equivalently, in local coordinates, convergence of the metric coefficients and all partial derivatives up to order k). Is the subset of R^k(M) consisting of metrics whose geodesic flow has positive topological entropy dense in R^k(M) with respect to this C^k-topology?
justification: The draft matches only the opening hypothesis "Assume M is closed," and this exact opening occurs three times in a row in §8.3, for Questions 8.3.1, 8.3.2, and 8.3.3. Because the draft gives no distinguishing words such as "entropy," "transitive," or "closed geodesics," it is too incomplete to identify a unique target with certainty. I therefore choose the first exact official formulation sharing that opening phrase, namely Question 8.3.1. The surrounding context immediately before that question defines the ambient space of metrics and the weak C^k-topology, which are essential to make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
